auth: Production API Gateway JWT authorizer validates Cognito ID token issuer/audience. Authenticated routes require sub, email, email_verified=true and token_use=id claims. Browser sends the Bearer ID token; tenant identity, Cognito deletion username, profile email and optional initial profile name come only from verified claims, not request bodies. Stored profile edits remain authoritative. Health, bounded guest onboarding routes and the signature-verified Stripe webhook are public. The CloudFront API origin policy sets CloudFront-Viewer-Address from trusted connection data and overwrites a viewer-supplied copy. The origin adds a private credential. Lambda accepts the normalized viewer IP for guest rate limits only after the origin credential succeeds; a gated guest request without a valid viewer address fails closed. Local synthetic account exists only when ROLECLUE_LOCAL_DEMO=1 is explicit and no AWS runtime is used.
configEndpoint: GET /config.json returns {apiBaseUrl,cognitoRegion,cognitoClientId,mode,marketingUrl,capabilities,betaNotice} with no secrets. Production defaults: apiBaseUrl='', cognitoRegion='ap-southeast-2', mode='production', marketingUrl='https://proairesis.digital'. capabilities.jobImport is true; recommendations, guestDiscovery, coverLetters and billing require the corresponding ROLECLUE_RECOMMENDATIONS_ENABLED, ROLECLUE_GUEST_DISCOVERY_ENABLED, ROLECLUE_COVER_LETTERS_ENABLED and ROLECLUE_BILLING_ENABLED release flags to equal 'true'. The signed-out guest journey is available only when both recommendations and guestDiscovery are true; otherwise the browser opens account access and the signed-in import flow. betaNotice starts with the job-import guidance and adds the discovery or subscription exclusion when that capability is disabled. Public flags and betaNotice control presentation, not server authorization or paid entitlement. Local mode=demo must be visibly labelled and is accepted by the browser only on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1].

profileOptionalFields.termsAcceptedAt: ISO timestamp recorded by the server when PUT /api/profile receives termsAccepted:true; absent until accepted.
profileOptionalFields.marketingConsent: Boolean when supplied; separate from resume-processing consent and terms acceptance.
profileOptionalFields.interviewCompleted: Boolean set only after the user reviews the guided interview summary. An explicit unknown work-rights or sponsorship answer remains valid.
profileOptionalFields.resumeObjectKey: Private S3 object key or null after successful parsing; not a download URL.
profileOptionalFields.resumeUploadId: Signed-upload ID, or null for the base64 route, after successful parsing.
profileOptionalFields.resumeOriginalExpiresAt: ISO timestamp seven days after saving an original, or null when no original is stored; indicates scheduled retention, not exact S3 deletion time.
profileOptionalFields.preferences.locationsRequired: Boolean hard location preference when supplied.
profileOptionalFields.preferences.workplaceRequired: Boolean hard workplace preference when supplied.
profileOptionalFields.preferences.minimumSalaryRequired: Boolean hard comparable-salary preference when supplied.

profileRules: PUT merges supported fields into the stored profile but always sets confirmed to whether input.confirmed is exactly true. interviewCompleted must be boolean when supplied and becomes true whenever the profile is confirmed. A confirmed profile stored before contract v4 is treated as interview-complete when its resume is replaced, so an existing member is not sent through the new interview again. termsAccepted is an input flag, not a stored profile field. Upload requires consent:true; successful parsing sets consentAt server-side, replaces resume text and detected skills, and clears confirmed. Confirmation requires resumeText, location, at least one roleFamily, consentAt and termsAcceptedAt. Client-supplied consentAt, termsAcceptedAt, termsVersion and resume storage fields are not writable. resumeText is at most 180000 UTF-8 bytes; the serialized profile is at most 220 KiB. Name, location and clearance are trimmed to 250 characters; skills are at most 60 strings of 200 characters; preference arrays are at most 20 strings of 200 characters; limitations are at most 2000 characters; yearsExperience must be finite and between 0 and 70 or becomes null.
guestInterviewRules: Guest start accepts only the interview fields shown above. The legacy {situation,location,remote} body remains valid and defaults interviewCompleted to false, roleFamilies to an empty array and eligibility answers to unknown. A completed interview requires a non-empty location, one to three supported role families, a boolean remote answer, and explicit work-rights and sponsorship answers; unknown is a valid explicit answer. Location is at most 250 characters, visaLimitations at most 1000 characters and limitations at most 2000 characters. Control characters, unsupported roles, duplicate roles, invalid enums, invalid types and unknown fields are rejected. Resume extraction never infers work rights, sponsorship or visa limitations. Interview answers win when present; the resume fills only missing evidence fields such as name, skills, experience, location and role direction.
applicationRules: An application stores one job snapshot; application.match contains the matching result without a duplicate job. GET /api/applications and PATCH /api/applications/:id return job.availability, job.availabilityMessage and job.availabilityCheckedAt. Availability is evaluated against the same tenant-bound recommendation snapshot that supplied the job, or against the user-provided import; an unrelated legacy feed cannot close a recommendation. Availability is closed if expiresAt has passed or the job is missing from a complete current snapshot for its source, available if present, and unknown when source freshness or completeness cannot be confirmed. Ignored decisions retain a bounded assessment snapshot so the opportunity remains restorable after a daily refresh. Application status is user-managed and separate from employer-job availability. Closed jobs keep saved applications and letters but reject new generation with 409 OPPORTUNITY_CLOSED. Notes are trimmed to 10000 characters; letter edits must contain 1 to 16000 trimmed characters.
billingRules: The free workspace has no cover-letter generation allowance. Starter is a one-time A$1 payment for two successful lifetime generations. It is available only while both starterEverPaid and subscriptionEverPaid are false; a refund never restores eligibility. Starter access is granted only after Stripe reports a complete paid Checkout Session whose customer, account reference, fixed server price, one line item and successful PaymentIntent all match. A full refund or dispute revokes unused Starter access but does not remove saved letters. The A$20 monthly subscription grants 50 successful generations only when canonical Stripe state links the current tenant, customer, subscription, configured monthly Price, non-prorated billing-period line, invoice, InvoicePayment, succeeded PaymentIntent and captured charge. The current invoice must show exactly A$20 paid in AUD through Stripe, with no discount, credit, balance application, off-Stripe amount or automatic tax. A paid status alone and a zero-value invoice grant nothing. Trialing alone grants no allowance and checkout creates no trial. Monthly credits are consumed before Starter credits, and unused Starter credits remain available after Plus ends. Monthly counters reset only when the canonical Stripe subscription billing-period key changes; unused monthly allowance does not roll over. remaining subtracts used and reserved. subscriptionStatus is separate from effective access status. A full monthly refund or dispute revokes the current monthly allowance while an ongoing subscription remains manageable; period-end cancellation preserves paid access until expiry. Active or otherwise managed RoleClue subscriptions identified by a stored subscription ID, the current fixed Price or tenant metadata remain manageable and block duplicate checkout and account deletion, including subscriptions on older offers or with legacy metadata. They never receive the current allowance without exact current-offer evidence. subscriptionEverPaid requires a positive verified Stripe payment, not an invoice status alone. hasSubscription requires a subscription ID and subscriptionStatus (falling back to status) in active, trialing, past_due, unpaid, incomplete, paused, refunded or payment_pending. canManageBilling indicates a stored Stripe customer ID. canGenerate describes allowance only, not provider availability, profile readiness or job availability. Legacy unspent free credit is ignored, while an already-reserved legacy generation may finish safely. Missing provider or either billing price configuration returns SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE. Public config and browser redirects never grant entitlement.
routes: GET /api/me => {profile,billing,feed:{status,lastUpdatedAt,message},capabilities:{jobImport,recommendations,guestDiscovery,coverLetters,billing},mode}; server capabilities reflect feed readiness, guest discovery availability, provider availability and billing configuration
PUT /api/profile body supported profile fields plus optional {termsAccepted:true,marketingConsent:boolean} => {profile}

POST /api/resume body {filename,contentType,dataBase64,consent:true} => {profile,extractedText,warnings:[]}; PDF/DOCX only; decoded maximum 5 MiB in demo and 3 MiB in production (larger production files return 413 DIRECT_UPLOAD_REQUIRED)

POST /api/resume/upload body {filename,contentType,size,consent:true} => {uploadId,uploadUrl,headers:{'Content-Type':contentType}}; size is integer bytes from 1 through 5 MiB; PDF/DOCX filename and MIME must agree
POST /api/resume/finalize body {uploadId} => {profile,extractedText,warnings:[]}; validates this user's uploaded bytes and declared size before saving; upload record must be no older than one hour

POST /api/guest/start body {situation,location,remote,roleFamilies?,workRights?,needsSponsorship?,visaLimitations?,limitations?,interviewCompleted?} => {guest}; creates a short-lived opaque guest session subject to IP-hash rate limits; the legacy three-field body remains valid

POST /api/guest/resume body {token,filename,contentType,dataBase64,consent:true,interview?} => {guest}; interview optionally contains the same bounded interview fields so edits made after Back are persisted before extraction; PDF/DOCX only, non-empty decoded maximum 4 MiB because this bounded signed-out path uses inline JSON transport
PUT or POST /api/guest/profile body {token,profile,termsAccepted:true} => {guest}; confirms only essential resume-derived fields plus work rights, sponsorship and user-entered limitations
POST /api/guest/search body {token} => {guest}; returns no more than five high-fit Australian technology roles from the approved current source
POST /api/guest/ignore body {token,jobId} => {guest}; preserves ignored role evidence for later restoration
POST /api/guest/claim body {token,interestedJobId} => {application,continuation}; requires verified account auth and atomically claims one guest session into that tenant

POST /api/guest/abandon body {token} => {abandoned:true,account}; requires verified account auth and marks a conflicting confirmed guest session resolved without copying its profile or resume into the existing tenant; a claimed session cannot be abandoned
GET /api/opportunities => {opportunities:[match],feed,excludedCount}; max 30

POST /api/opportunities/refresh => {opportunities:[match],feed,excludedCount}; requests a current authorised-source refresh before returning the authenticated user's reranked high-fit shortlist; max 30
GET /api/ignored => {opportunities:[match],feed,excludedCount}; max 30
POST /api/opportunities/:id/decision body {decision:'interested'|'ignored'|'undecided'} => {application?}
GET /api/applications => {applications:[application]}
PATCH /api/applications/:id body {status?,notes?} => {application}

POST /api/applications/:id/letters header Idempotency-Key matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{16,100}$ => {generation,billing}; 202 pending, otherwise 200; 402 STARTER_REQUIRED, UPGRADE_REQUIRED or ALLOWANCE_EXHAUSTED; 409 OPPORTUNITY_CLOSED; 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE when generation is disabled
GET /api/generations/:id => {generation,billing}
PATCH /api/applications/:id/letters/:letterId body {text} => {letter}

POST /api/billing/checkout body {plan:'starter'|'monthly'|'prepaid',termsAccepted:true} => {url}; plan defaults to monthly for compatibility. The server maps plans to fixed active Stripe prices, uses mode=payment for A$1 Starter and mode=subscription for A$20 monthly, uses the merchant's dashboard-managed payment methods, collects a payment method for monthly checkout, requires terms consent, explicitly disables automatic tax, supplies no manual tax rates, and enables no trial, promotion code or discount. A successful Checkout returns to /?checkout=success&plan=starter#account or /?checkout=success&plan=monthly#account so the client confirms only the purchased offer. Cached Checkout state stores and verifies the plan, current price, current terms and disabled automatic-tax state before reuse; mismatched open sessions are expired. Stripe idempotency keys include the explicit Checkout request-contract version and offer version, so retries of one current request remain stable without colliding with a legacy request shape. Starter returns 409 STARTER_NOT_ELIGIBLE after any successful Starter or Plus payment.
POST /api/billing/portal => {url}

POST /api/billing/refresh => {billing}; authenticated active account, canonical Stripe reconciliation; 10-second per-user throttle returns 429 BILLING_REFRESH_LIMIT; 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE if reconciliation is not configured
POST /api/stripe/webhook raw body/signature; no user auth; verified Stripe signature and canonical re-fetch for checkout completion/expiry, subscription and invoice changes, full refunds and disputes
GET /api/export => {exportedAt,records:[{type,value}]}; authenticated user's DynamoDB records excluding UPLOAD# records; does not download original files
DELETE /api/account body {confirmation:'DELETE'} => {deleted:true}; deletion fences and retry behavior are specified in deletion below
GET /api/health => {ok,mode}; non-sensitive liveness only
uploads: The signed-in production browser starts a signed upload, PUTs up to 5 MiB of raw file bytes to uploadUrl using the returned Content-Type header, then finalizes by uploadId. The URL is a five-minute, size- and content-type-bound private S3 PUT grant, not an API route or public download. The signed-out guest path accepts up to 4 MiB inline so the base64 JSON plus gateway event remains below Lambda's synchronous payload limit. Each authenticated user can start five uploads per Sydney calendar day, including attempts that later fail. Finalization is idempotent only while the processed upload is still the current resume; a replaced processed upload returns 409 UPLOAD_ALREADY_PROCESSED. Concurrent finalization returns 409 UPLOAD_PROCESSING; invalid files require a new upload. Validated bytes are copied into a new private original object so a live pending-object grant cannot alter the saved original.
storage: Production DynamoDB uses USER#sub partitions and separate profile, decisions, applications, letters, generations and entitlement records. Every stored item, including keys, revision and optional TTL, is guarded at 350 KiB of serialized UTF-8 JSON before writing; oversized items return 413 RECORD_TOO_LARGE. Profile limit is separately 220 KiB. Normalized jobs are at most 90000 serialized UTF-8 bytes, with descriptions at most 30000 characters and 60000 UTF-8 bytes. Shared authorized job snapshots are separate from user data. CAS/transactions protect quota and deletion fences. Original resumes are private S3 objects. Local memory storage is for explicitly selected synthetic demo data.
retention: Resume-bucket lifecycle rules expire pending/ objects after one day and users/ original resumes after seven days; lifecycle execution is asynchronous. Upload records have a two-day DynamoDB TTL, upload-rate records eight days; TTL removal is asynchronous. Resume text and account records have no automatic inactivity expiry and remain until account deletion. Terminal generation records drop profile/job snapshots; unresolved pending generations retain them until reconciliation. Lambda/API logs retain 30 days. DynamoDB point-in-time recovery uses a seven-day recovery period, so deletion is not immediate removal from backups. Replacing a resume attempts immediate deletion of the previous original; failure leaves the seven-day lifecycle as fallback.
deletion: Requires confirmation:'DELETE'. Returns 409 GENERATION_PENDING for pending generations or reserved allowance, UPLOAD_GRANT_ACTIVE until seven minutes after the latest signed-upload start, CHECKOUT_PENDING while a checkout lock or any tenant-owned current or legacy Stripe Checkout payment remains open, processing or indeterminate, and CANCEL_SUBSCRIPTION_FIRST while a linked current or legacy RoleClue subscription is active, trialing, past_due, unpaid, incomplete or paused. The server queries canonical Stripe Checkout, PaymentIntent and subscription state; local checkout expiry never proves settlement. A terminal failed or canceled Starter payment permits deletion. A successful exact current-offer payment is reconciled before deletion continues; a succeeded legacy payment permits deletion only after its session, customer and PaymentIntent ownership are verified. Scheduled cancellation alone does not permit deletion before paid access ends. A transaction installs DELETING and a durable hashed-subject tombstone while checking entitlement, checkout and upload-state revisions; all user writes check these fences. Other authenticated routes then reject ACCOUNT_DELETING or ACCOUNT_DELETED. DELETE remains retryable after a partial failure. Completion removes the user's pending/original S3 objects and linked guest partitions, removes USER#sub records, then revokes the exact verified Cognito username (including federated identities). The hashed tombstone remains to reject still-valid old tokens; external Stripe records and separate billing mappings are not included in USER partition deletion.
generation: Production reserves allowance and writes a tenant-bound pending-generation outbox record in the same DynamoDB transaction before dispatching an asynchronous worker with the server-derived generation ID. A bounded, durable two-pass migration enrolls pending generations created before the outbox release and waits between passes so pre-release Lambda executions cannot miss enrollment. A five-minute schedule scans at most 50 outbox records per page and sends an opaque continuation cursor through the generation queue. It retries only pre-provider work whose dispatch and worker leases are no longer active. Provider-started work is never dispatched or generated again; an expired provider-started lease stays pending with pendingReason=PROVIDER_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and emits an operator reconciliation event. Successful and definitive-failure completion removes the outbox record in the terminal transaction. Local demo may finish immediately. Public generation includes id, appId, status, createdAt, bucket and periodKey; terminal results add completedAt plus letter or error. Internal snapshots, leases, dispatch fields and the outbox are excluded from user responses and exports. A successful stored letter consumes allowance; a definitive failure releases its reservation. Idempotent replay returns the same generation; using that key for another application returns 409 KEY_ALREADY_USED. Missing provider returns SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE without reserving allowance. Synthetic templates exist only in explicit local demo mode.
serviceGates: Production mode does not imply public launch readiness. Freehire discovery requires FREEHIRE_ENABLED=true, FREEHIRE_LICENSE_APPROVED=true and an evidence reference for its public API. A separate licensed feed requires JOB_FEED_LICENSE_APPROVED=true and configured source registry or licensed feed URL/reference. An unconfigured source returns an honest unavailable state and no sample jobs. Provider enablement requires OPENAI_API_KEY_PARAM, the pinned OPENAI_MODEL and positive daily call/token limits. RoleClue also enforces a hard US$1 daily AI spend ceiling inside the approved shared budget. Billing requires the Stripe secret, webhook-secret parameter, a versioned active AUD 2000 monthly Price ID and a separate active AUD 100 one-time Starter Price ID. These server gates operate independently of public config and betaNotice.
frontend: React JSX + Vite with plain CSS. RoleClue cream #fbf4e8, deep teal #062f3b, coral #ff805f, mint #85c5ae, Georgia headings and Avenir Next body. Config and API/auth adapters are in src/. The API adapter adds httpStatus client-side; it is not a server response field. Production has no synthetic fallback.

prepaidWalletPayments.verification: Canonical Stripe Checkout, line item, PaymentIntent and captured charge must match owner, offer, A$20 and terms version. No browser redirect grants access. Refunds or disputes revoke access; repeated reconciliation preserves counters. Prepaid periods cannot stack with active paid periods or subscriptions. Merchant wallet activation approval is separate from deployment.
